subject: grapes in microwave
title: What If You Microwaved Two Grapes?

scenes.text: What if you put two grapes in a microwave? You'd make the same glowing stuff as lightning.
Within seconds, a bright flash of plasma bursts out where the two grapes touch.
Scientists in Canada finally explained it in 2019. Each grape traps microwaves like a tiny echo chamber.
Microwaves are about 12 centimeters long in air, but inside water they shrink to roughly grape size.
Two touching grapes squeeze that energy into one tiny hotspot, hot enough to rip sodium and potassium into glowing plasma.
Water beads with no skin did the same. And the scientists' advice: don't try it. You could melt a hole in your microwave.

description:
A 2019 PNAS study by Khattak, Bianucci and Slepkov showed that grape-sized water spheres act as microwave resonators; two touching grapes concentrate the energy into a hotspot at the contact point that ionizes sodium and potassium into plasma. Skinless hydrogel beads did the same.
The researchers warn it can damage a microwave oven.
What should we run through next?
